lessons.title: Choosing a career
lessons.goal: I can talk about choosing a career.

newItems.definition: A person or company that pays people to work.
newItems.example: Her employer gives her two weeks off.

newItems.definition: A strong wish to do well or to be successful.
newItems.example: His ambition is to run his own shop.

newItems.definition: A job that needs special study or training, like law or teaching.
newItems.example: Nursing is a caring profession.

newItems.definition: To move to better and better jobs over time.
newItems.example: She wants to climb the career ladder fast.

newItems.definition: To move to better jobs slowly by working hard.
newItems.example: He worked his way up from shop assistant to manager.

mainWord.definition: A person or company that pays people to work.
mainWord.example: Her employer gives her two weeks off.

lessons.mainWordForms: Employer is a noun. A person or company that pays people to work. Her employer gives her two weeks off.
lessons.expression: She wants to climb the career ladder fast.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about moving to better jobs over time.
lessons.expressionTask: Maya talks to Daniel about his career. What does she want to do?
lessons.grammar: Present perfect continuous: I have been working as a designer for five years
lessons.pattern: I have been working as a designer for five years.
lessons.task: I have been ___ as a designer for five years.
lessons.example: I have been working as a designer for five years.
context: Maya talks to Daniel about choosing a career.
She wants to climb the career ladder fast. Daniel started at the bottom and worked his way up.
dialogue: Maya: Daniel, what is your ambition for the next five years?
Daniel: I want to climb the career ladder. I have been working as an analyst for two years.
Maya: That is a good ambition. What is your employer like?
Daniel: Carter Retail Group is a good employer. I started at the bottom and worked my way up.
Priya: Teaching is a good profession too. My sister is a teacher.
Maya: Yes. Choose a career you love, and work your way up step by step.
lessons.listening: On Monday, Daniel talks to Maya about choosing a career. His ambition is to climb the career ladder and become a manager. He has been working as an analyst for two years. His employer is Carter Retail Group. Maya says, 'Teaching is a good profession too. Choose a career you love. Start at the bottom and work your way up.' Daniel is happy.
lessons.question: What is Daniel's ambition?
lessons.correct: To climb the career ladder and become a manager
lessons.other: To leave his job at once
lessons.reading: On Monday, Daniel talks to Maya about choosing a career. Daniel works for Carter Retail Group. His ambition is to climb the career ladder and become a manager one day. He has been working as an analyst for two years. His employer is a good company, and his team is friendly. Maya says, 'Choose a career you love. Teaching is a good profession, but business is good too.' Daniel asks, 'How can I climb the career ladder fast?' Maya says, 'Start at the bottom and work your way up. Learn new skills every year. Talk to people in other teams. Ask your boss for new work.' Priya says, 'My sister is a teacher. Her profession makes her happy. She worked her way up from a small school to a big one.' Maya says, 'Good. Work hard, learn fast, and climb the career ladder step by step.' Daniel is happy. He says, 'Thank you, Maya. I will work hard every day.'
lessons.readingQ: What does Maya tell Daniel to do?
lessons.readingA: Start at the bottom and work his way up.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about choosing a career. What is your ambition? What job do you want?
lessons.speakingSample: I want to talk about choosing a career. My ambition is to climb the career ladder and become a manager. I have been working as an analyst for two years. My employer is Carter Retail Group. Teaching is a good profession too. I will start at the bottom and work my way up. I will learn new skills every year.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them about the career you want. Say what your ambition is and how you will reach it.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Tom, I want to tell you about choosing a career. My ambition is to climb the career ladder and become a manager. I have been working as an analyst for two years. My employer is Carter Retail Group. Teaching is a good profession too. I will start at the bottom and work my way up. I will learn new skills every year. Please tell me about your career. What is your ambition for the next five years? Best, Daniel
lessons.sound: Employer has its strongest beat on PLOY. In employer, say PLOY clearly in the middle. In ambition, say BI clearly in the middle.
lessons.model: Her employer gives her two weeks off.
lessons.wordSample: My employer is Carter Retail Group.

lessons.title: Job interviews
lessons.goal: I can talk about job interviews.

newItems.definition: A person who asks for a job by sending in an application.
newItems.example: Ten applicants came for the interview.

newItems.definition: The person who asks questions at a job interview.
newItems.example: The interviewer asked about her last job.

newItems.definition: A person who is being considered for a job.
newItems.example: Three candidates will come for a second interview.

newItems.definition: To get a job, often after trying hard.
newItems.example: She landed a job at a big bank.

newItems.definition: To attend a meeting to be asked about a job.
newItems.example: She will go for an interview on Monday.

mainWord.definition: A person who asks for a job by sending in an application.
mainWord.example: Ten applicants came for the interview.

lessons.mainWordForms: Applicant is a noun. A person who asks for a job by sending in an application. Ten applicants came for the interview.
lessons.expression: She landed a job at a big bank.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about getting a job after trying hard.
lessons.expressionTask: Priya tells Daniel about her last interview. Where did she land a job?
lessons.grammar: Indirect questions: Could you tell me about your last job
lessons.pattern: Could you tell me about your last job?
lessons.task: Could you tell me ___ your last job?
lessons.example: Could you tell me about your last job?
context: Priya tells Daniel about her last interview.
She landed a job at a big bank. The interviewer asked about her last job.
dialogue: Priya: Daniel, I will go for an interview at a big bank next week.
Daniel: Good luck. Could you tell me about your last job?
Priya: I will tell the interviewer about my work. She will ask many questions.
Daniel: Will there be one other candidate for the job?
Priya: Yes, but I am a strong applicant. I hope to land a job there.
Maya: Well done. It is not easy to land a job at a big bank.
lessons.listening: On Tuesday, Priya tells Daniel about her interview. She will go for an interview. One other candidate will come too. The interviewer will ask about her last job. Daniel asks, 'Could you tell me about your last job?' Priya says, 'I worked at a small bank for two years. I was a strong applicant.' Maya says, 'It is not easy to land a job.'
lessons.question: Where will Priya go for an interview?
lessons.reading: On Tuesday, Priya tells Daniel about her interview. She will go for an interview at a big bank next week. She hopes to land a job there. The interviewer will ask about her last job. Daniel asks, 'Could you tell me about your last job?' Priya says, 'I worked at a small bank for two years. I was a strong applicant. One other candidate will come for the job too.' Maya says, 'Good luck. It is not easy to land a job at a big bank. Tell the interviewer about your work. Answer in full sentences. Ask about the team and the hours.' Priya says, 'Thank you. I will go for an interview on Monday morning. I hope I can land a job at the bank.' Daniel says, 'You will do well. You are a strong applicant.' Maya is happy. She says, 'Good. A good interview starts with a good plan.'
lessons.readingQ: What will the interviewer ask about?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a job interview. What did the interviewer ask? How did you answer?
lessons.speakingSample: I want to tell you about a job interview. I will go for an interview at a big bank next week. The interviewer will ask about my last job. I was a strong applicant at a small bank. One other candidate will come too. I hope to land a job there. I will tell the interviewer about my work. Wish me luck.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them about a job interview you will go for. Say where it is and how you will prepare.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about a job interview. I will go for an interview at a big bank next week. The interviewer will ask about my last job. I was a strong applicant at a small bank for two years. One other candidate will come for the job too. I hope to land a job there. I will tell the interviewer about my work. Please wish me luck. Thank you. Best, Priya
lessons.sound: Applicant has its strongest beat on AP. In applicant, say AP clearly at the start. In interviewer, say IN clearly at the start.
lessons.model: The applicant waited in the hall.
lessons.wordTask: Who asks the questions at an interview?

lessons.title: Changing careers
lessons.goal: I can talk about changing careers.

newItems.definition: Working for different companies, not for one employer.
newItems.example: She is a freelance writer now.

newItems.definition: The loss of a job because the work is no longer needed.
newItems.example: The factory closed and many workers faced redundancy.

newItems.definition: To start working in a different area from before.
newItems.example: At forty, he made a career change.

newItems.definition: To begin something again, with nothing from before.
newItems.example: After the move, she started from scratch.

newItems.definition: To try to reach a big and difficult goal.
newItems.example: Aim high, and you may get the top job.

mainWord.definition: Working for different companies, not for one employer.
mainWord.example: She is a freelance writer now.

lessons.mainWordForms: Freelance is an adjective. Working for different companies, not for one employer. She is a freelance writer now.
lessons.expression: At forty, he made a career change.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about starting work in a different area.
lessons.expressionTask: Daniel thinks about a new career. When did he make a career change?
lessons.grammar: Future in the past: I was going to change jobs last year
lessons.pattern: I was going to change jobs last year.
lessons.task: I was going to ___ jobs last year.
lessons.example: I was going to change jobs last year.
context: Daniel thinks about a career change.
At forty, he made a career change. He will start from scratch in a new town.
dialogue: Daniel: Maya, I was going to change jobs last year, but I stayed.
Maya: Do you want to make a career change now?
Daniel: Yes. I want to be freelance and work for different firms.
Priya: My old firm had a redundancy last year. Many workers left.
Daniel: That is hard. I will start from scratch in a new town.
Maya: Good. Aim high. A new start can be the best start.
lessons.listening: On Wednesday, Daniel talks to Maya about changing careers. He was going to change jobs last year. Now he wants to make a career change. He wants to be freelance and work for different firms. Priya says her old firm had a redundancy last year. Daniel says, 'I will start from scratch in a new town.' Maya says, 'Aim high. Good luck.'
lessons.question: What does Daniel want to do now?
lessons.reading: On Wednesday, Daniel talks to Maya about changing careers. He was going to change jobs last year, but he stayed at the bank. Now he wants to make a career change. He wants to be freelance and work for different firms. Maya asks, 'Why do you want to change?' Daniel says, 'I want new work and new people. I was going to change jobs last year, but I was afraid.' Priya says, 'My old firm had a redundancy last year. Many good workers left. One friend started from scratch in a new town.' Maya says, 'A new start can be good. But plan first. Save money, learn new skills, and talk to people in the new area.' Daniel says, 'Thank you. I will start from scratch and work hard. I want to be freelance by next year.' Maya is happy. She says, 'Good. Make a plan, aim high, and make a career change step by step.'
lessons.readingQ: Why did Daniel not change jobs last year?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about changing careers. What new work do you want? Why?
lessons.speakingSample: I want to talk about changing careers. I was going to change jobs last year, but I stayed. Now I want to make a career change. I want to be freelance and work for different firms. I will start from scratch in a new town. A redundancy at my old firm made me think. Aim high. A new start can be the best start.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them you want to make a career change. Say what new work you want and why.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Lisa, I want to tell you about changing careers. I was going to change jobs last year, but I stayed. Now I want to make a career change. I want to be freelance and work for different firms. I will start from scratch in a new town. A redundancy at my old firm made me think. Aim high. A new start can be the best start. I will plan first and save money. Please tell me what you think. Best, Daniel
lessons.sound: Freelance has its strongest beat on FREE. In freelance, say FREE clearly at the start. In redundancy, say DUN clearly in the middle.
lessons.model: She is a freelance writer now.
lessons.wordTask: What does a freelance worker do?
lessons.wordSample: A freelance worker works for different firms.

lessons.title: Skills and strengths
lessons.goal: I can talk about my skills and strengths.

newItems.definition: A certificate or exam pass that shows you can do a job.
newItems.example: You need a teaching qualification for this job.

newItems.definition: Working hard at something because you care about it.
newItems.example: Her dedication to her work is clear.

newItems.definition: Trying hard for a long time and not giving up.
newItems.example: Success needs perseverance.

newItems.definition: To use what you are good at in your work.
newItems.example: In the interview, play to your strengths.

newItems.definition: To try to get better at the things you are not good at.
newItems.example: He works on his weaknesses every week.

mainWord.definition: A certificate or exam pass that shows you can do a job.
mainWord.example: You need a teaching qualification for this job.

lessons.mainWordForms: Qualification is a noun. A certificate or exam pass that shows you can do a job. You need a teaching qualification for this job.
lessons.expression: In the interview, play to your strengths.
lessons.use: Use this when you tell someone to use what they are good at.
lessons.expressionTask: Maya talks to Daniel about his skills. What should he do in the interview?
lessons.grammar: Be used to and get used to: I am used to early starts
lessons.pattern: I am used to early starts.
lessons.example: I am used to early starts.
context: Maya talks to Daniel about his skills.
In the interview, play to your strengths. Work on your weaknesses every week.
dialogue: Maya: Daniel, what is your best qualification for the new job?
Daniel: I have a teaching qualification, and I am used to early starts.
Priya: Good. Your dedication is clear. You work hard every day.
Daniel: Thank you. Perseverance is my best skill. I never give up.
Maya: In the interview, play to your strengths. Work on your weaknesses every week.
Priya: Yes. I will get used to the new system soon.
lessons.listening: On Thursday, Maya talks to Daniel about his skills. Daniel has a teaching qualification. His dedication is clear. He works hard. Maya says, 'In the interview, play to your strengths. Work on your weaknesses every week.' Daniel says, 'Perseverance is my best skill. I never give up. I am used to early starts.' Priya says, 'Good. You will get used to the new system soon.'
lessons.question: What is Daniel's best skill?
lessons.reading: On Thursday, Maya talks to Daniel about his skills. Daniel has a teaching qualification. His dedication is clear to all his team. He works hard every day and never gives up. Maya says, 'In the interview, play to your strengths. Tell them about your teaching qualification. Work on your weaknesses every week, and you will get better.' Daniel says, 'Perseverance is my best skill. I am used to early starts, and I will get used to the new system soon.' Priya says, 'Good. My best skill is clear writing. I work on my weaknesses too. I take a class every month.' Maya says, 'That is smart. Play to your strengths at work, and work on your weaknesses at home.' Daniel is happy. He says, 'Thank you, Maya. I will play to my strengths in the interview.'
lessons.readingQ: What does Maya tell Daniel to do in the interview?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about your skills. What are your strengths? What do you want to get better at?
lessons.speakingSample: I want to tell you about my skills. I have a teaching qualification. My dedication is clear. I work hard every day. Perseverance is my best skill. I never give up. In the interview, I will play to my strengths. I will work on my weaknesses every week. I am used to early starts. I will get used to the new system soon.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them about your skills and strengths. Say what you are good at and what you want to learn.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Tom, I want to tell you about my skills. I have a teaching qualification. My dedication is clear. I work hard every day. Perseverance is my best skill. I never give up. In the interview, I will play to my strengths. I will work on my weaknesses every week. I am used to early starts. I will get used to the new system soon. I learn fast and I help my team. Please tell me about your skills. Best, Daniel
lessons.sound: Qualification has its strongest beat on CA. In qualification, say CA clearly near the end. In dedication, say CA clearly in the middle.
lessons.model: You need a teaching qualification for this job.
lessons.wordSample: It is a certificate that shows you can do a job.

lessons.title: Work-life balance
lessons.goal: I can talk about work-life balance.

newItems.definition: Feeling very tired and unable to work well after too much work.
newItems.example: Too much overtime can lead to burnout.

newItems.definition: Something extra you get from your job, like free food.
newItems.example: Free lunch is a nice perk of the job.

newItems.definition: To find a good middle way between two things.
newItems.example: She tries to strike a balance between work and family.

newItems.definition: To work or study very late at night.
newItems.example: He burned the midnight oil before the big meeting.

newItems.definition: To stop work for a time, often for a holiday.
newItems.example: She will take time off next week.

mainWord.definition: Feeling very tired and unable to work well after too much work.
mainWord.example: Too much overtime can lead to burnout.

lessons.mainWordForms: Burnout is a noun. Feeling very tired and unable to work well after too much work. Too much overtime can lead to burnout.
lessons.expression: She tries to strike a balance between work and family.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about finding a good middle way.
lessons.expressionTask: Priya talks about work and life. What does she try to do?
lessons.grammar: Would rather and had better: I would rather work from home
lessons.pattern: I would rather work from home.
lessons.example: I would rather work from home.
context: Priya talks about work and life.
She tries to strike a balance between work and family. She will take time off next week.
dialogue: Priya: Maya, I am so busy. I work late every night.
Maya: Be careful. Too much work can lead to burnout.
Daniel: Yes. Try to strike a balance between work and family.
Priya: You are right. I will take time off next week.
Daniel: Good. A free lunch is a nice perk of the job, but rest is better.
Maya: Yes. Do not burn the midnight oil every night.
lessons.listening: On Friday, Priya talks to Maya about work and life. She is so busy. Maya says, 'Be careful. Too much work can lead to burnout. Try to strike a balance between work and family.' Priya says, 'I will take time off next week.' Daniel says, 'Good. Do not burn the midnight oil every night. A free lunch is a nice perk of the job.'
lessons.question: What will Priya do next week?
lessons.reading: On Friday, Priya talks to Maya about work and life. She is so busy. She works late every night, and she is tired. Maya says, 'Be careful. Too much work can lead to burnout. Try to strike a balance between work and family.' Priya says, 'You are right. I would rather work from home two days a week.' Daniel says, 'Good idea. I will take time off next week too. Do not burn the midnight oil every night. A free lunch is a nice perk of the job, but rest is better.' Maya says, 'Yes. Take time off when you need it. Work hard in the day, and rest at night.' Priya says, 'Thank you. I will strike a balance from now on. I will not burn the midnight oil every night.' Maya is happy. She says, 'Good. A happy worker is a good worker.'
lessons.readingQ: What does Maya say too much work can lead to?
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about work and life. How do you strike a balance? What do you do to rest?
lessons.speakingSample: I want to talk about work and life. I am so busy. I work late every night. Too much work can lead to burnout. I try to strike a balance between work and family. I will take time off next week. I do not burn the midnight oil every night now. A free lunch is a nice perk of the job.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them about your work and life. Say how you strike a balance and what you do to rest.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about work and life. I am so busy. I work late every night. Too much work can lead to burnout. I try to strike a balance between work and family. I will take time off next week. I do not burn the midnight oil every night now. A free lunch is a nice perk of the job. Please tell me how you rest. Take care. Write soon. Best, Priya
lessons.sound: Burnout has its strongest beat on BURN. In burnout, say BURN clearly at the start. In perk, say PERK clearly.
lessons.model: Too much overtime can lead to burnout.
lessons.wordSample: It is feeling very tired after too much work.

lessons.title: Promotion and ambition
lessons.goal: I can talk about promotion and ambition.

newItems.definition: A person with more experience who helps and advises you at work.
newItems.example: Her mentor helped her plan her career.

newItems.definition: Meeting people at work events to find new chances.
newItems.example: Networking helped him find a new job.

newItems.definition: Money paid to a worker for each thing they sell.
newItems.example: He earns a commission on every car he sells.

newItems.definition: To get a better job in the same company.
newItems.example: Hard work helps you move up the ladder.

newItems.definition: To be likely to get something good, like a promotion.
newItems.example: She is in line for a promotion.

mainWord.definition: A person with more experience who helps and advises you at work.
mainWord.example: Her mentor helped her plan her career.

lessons.mainWordForms: Mentor is a noun. A person with more experience who helps and advises you at work. Her mentor helped her plan her career.
lessons.expression: Hard work helps you move up the ladder.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about getting a better job in the same company.
lessons.expressionTask: Daniel talks to his mentor about a promotion. What helps you move up the ladder?

Daniel: Yes. I earn a commission on every sale now.
Maya: Well done. You are in line for a promotion.
lessons.listening: On Saturday, Daniel talks to his mentor about a promotion. He says, 'I do want that promotion. What should I do?' Maya says, 'Hard work helps you move up the ladder. lessons.question: What does Maya tell Daniel to do?

lessons.model: Her mentor helped her plan her career.
lessons.wordSample: A mentor is a person who helps you at work.

lessons.title: Starting your own business
lessons.goal: I can talk about starting your own business.

newItems.definition: A person who starts a new business and takes the risk.
newItems.example: The entrepreneur opened a small cafe.

newItems.definition: A new small business that is just beginning.
newItems.example: He works for a tech startup.

newItems.definition: To work for yourself, not for a company.
newItems.example: He wants to be his own boss.

newItems.definition: To start a new business.
newItems.example: They set up a business together.

newItems.definition: To do something big and risky after thinking about it.
newItems.example: She took the plunge and opened her own shop.

mainWord.definition: A person who starts a new business and takes the risk.
mainWord.example: The entrepreneur opened a small cafe.

lessons.mainWordForms: Entrepreneur is a noun. A person who starts a new business and takes the risk. The entrepreneur opened a small cafe.
lessons.expression: He wants to be his own boss.
lessons.use: Use this when you talk about working for yourself.
lessons.expressionTask: Maya talks about a new startup. What does he want to be?
lessons.grammar: Be about to: We are about to open our own shop
lessons.pattern: We are about to open our own shop.
lessons.task: We are about to ___ our own shop.
lessons.example: We are about to open our own shop.
context: Maya talks about a new startup.
He wants to be his own boss. They set up a business together.

Daniel: What does he do? Is his startup doing well?
Maya: Yes. He wants to be his own boss. They set up a business together.
Daniel: That takes courage. Did he take the plunge at once?
Priya: No. He planned for a year. We are about to open our own shop too.
Maya: Good. A new startup needs a good plan.
lessons.listening: On Sunday, Maya talks about a new startup. She met an entrepreneur at the market. He wants to be his own boss. They set up a business together. Daniel asks, 'Did he take the plunge at once?' Priya says, 'No. He planned for a year. We are about to open our own shop too. A new startup needs a good plan.'
lessons.question: Did the entrepreneur take the plunge at once?
lessons.correct: No, he planned for a year
lessons.reading: On Sunday, Maya talks about a new startup. She met an entrepreneur at the market yesterday. He wants to be his own boss. They set up a business together last year. lessons.readingQ: What did the entrepreneur do before he started?

lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them about a business you want to start. Say what it is and how you will start it.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Lisa, I want to tell you about starting my own business. I met an entrepreneur at the market. He wants to be his own boss. They set up a business together.
